big_picture: Test whether changing the economic/statistical target reveals stronger structure than generic next-session returns.

historical_facts.does_not_rule_out: Volatility or event mechanisms with materially more effective information, stronger effect size, or a different predeclared design.
historical_facts.observed: The HAR-style volatility diagnostic improved QLIKE by about 15.55% on 204 diagnostic rows, but protected confirmation was not opened because power gates showed detectable effects materially larger than the declared 5% MEPI.
historical_facts.rules_out: Claiming a confirmed volatility edge from the diagnostic or spending protected confirmation when the design is underpowered.

programme_interpretation: Volatility remains the strongest positive diagnostic observation, but both governed successor designs are information-limited. HOLD further experimentation; do not run another near-neighbour horizon/model variant.
revisit_trigger: Reopen only after a materially distinct design produces nuisance-only max relative-MDE/MEPI <= 1.0 across every predeclared dependence sensitivity and a fresh confirmation path is proven.
tested_role_target_horizon: Realized-volatility/variance diagnostics followed by power-gated volatility and event-specific confirmation designs.
useful_secondary_observations: Volatility persistence is the strongest positive diagnostic observation so far.
Calendar row count is not equivalent to effective independent information.
why_zoomed_in: Repeated return-model failures made target and mechanism selection more valuable than broader model search.
